record.original_question: Suppose f is a holomorphic map on P^2 of degree d ≥ 2. Must f have a repelling fixed point.

evidence.quote: Problem 10.3.1 Suppose f is a holomorphic map on P2 of degree d ≥ 2. Must f have a repelling fixed point.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $f:\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ be a holomorphic self-map of the complex projective plane of algebraic degree $d \geq 2$ (i.e., $f$ is induced by a triple of homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ in three variables with no common zero other than the origin). A fixed point $p$ of $f$ is said to be repelling if both eigenvalues of the differential $df_p$ (acting on the tangent space $T_p\mathbb{P}^2$) have modulus strictly greater than $1$. Must every such $f$ possess at least one repelling fixed point?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up extensive related results — e.g., the Briend–Duval theorem that repelling periodic points are dense in the Julia set of any holomorphic endomorphism of $\mathbb{P}^k$ of degree $\geq 2$, work by Guillot–Ramírez on multipliers at fixed points of quadratic self-maps of $\mathbb{P}^2$, and work by Berteloot–Bianchi on holomorphic motions of repelling cycles — but no source was found that explicitly resolves the question of whether every degree-$d\geq 2$ holomorphic self-map of $\mathbb{P}^2$ necessarily has a repelling fixed point. The current status could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Self-maps of projective space: Fixed-point theorems and multipliers
status_evidence.snippet: Talk on fixed-point theorems and multipliers for self-maps of projective space.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that fixed-point theorems and multipliers for self-maps of projective space remain an active research area, without an explicit resolution of the repelling fixed point question on P^2.

status_evidence.title: On the Multipliers at Fixed Points of Quadratic Self-Maps of the Projective Plane with an Invariant Line
status_evidence.snippet: A generic quadratic self-map of the projective plane with an invariant line is holomorphic and has seven different fixed points; the paper studies algebraic relations among eigenvalues at fixed points.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research focuses on multipliers at fixed points of holomorphic self-maps of P^2 but does not state the general existence of a repelling fixed point as established.

status_evidence.title: Stability and bifurcations in projective holomorphic dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses holomorphic motion of repelling periodic points for endomorphisms of P^k.
status_evidence.claim: Repelling periodic points (not necessarily fixed) are central; existence of a repelling fixed point on P^2 in degree d>=2 is not stated as a theorem here.
